ways.label: Marahau to Wainui

end.name: Wainui car park
end.quote: follows the estuary edge to the car park

via.name: saddle overlooking Wainui Inlet
via.quote: a saddle overlooking the serene Wainui Inlet

evidence: You’ll begin your journey as you cross the estuary over the Marahau causeway, and follow the track, first through open country, then lush beech forest with large kānuka trees.
The track winds down to the shore and follows the estuary edge to the car park.
Most visitors only walk in one direction on the Coast Track and get a water taxi in the other direction.

ways.label: Whariwharangi Bay to Tōtaranui

via.name: low saddle overlooking Wainui Inlet
via.quote: a low saddle overlooking Wainui Inlet

evidence: From Whariwharangi Hut follow a small stream, then climb out of the bay to a low saddle overlooking Wainui Inlet.
At this point take a left turn onto the Gibbs Hill Track.
This track will take you over the steep Gibbs Hill then back down to Tōtaranui.
Visitors travelling beyond Totaranui use the Gibbs Hill Track to make a loop in the Northern end of the Park.

not_on_route.quote: It is also possible to access Awaroa estuary on a road that is 31 km from Takaka.

doubts: The page says the track can be walked in either direction; it is recorded south to north (Marahau to Wainui) as the sections describe it. Start ref F3 (Coast Track meets Harvey Road) is the only southern Coast Track road end among the features; the text names the place only as Marahau, not the road. No feature is clearly the Wainui car park (F1 is the Taupo Point Track, not the Coast Track), so the end ref is null. The Anchorage to Bark Bay leg has a high tide track and a low tide crossing of Torrent Bay estuary; the Bark Bay estuary also has an all-tide track; near Awaroa there is a non-DOC track to the beach for water taxis; these alternatives are not recorded as separate ways. W2 (Whariwharangi Bay to Tōtaranui over Gibbs Hill) is recorded as an alternative ending; its time and distance are for that section only; 'Gibbs Hill Track' may be map track T7 'Gibbs Track' but this is not certain. Water taxi pickup locations (Apple Tree Bay, Anchorage, Medlands Bay, Bark Bay, Tonga Quarry, Onetahuti, Awaroa, Totaranui) could also be places to join the walk but are not recorded as access points. Kaiteretere is listed as an entrance but by kayak or water taxi only. The 5-7 day circuit using the Inland Track is treated as another walk.
